scope: High-synthesis-relevance historical excludes from 2026-09-19..2026-10-12 existing reviews, prioritized from exact titles and rechecked on primary Crossref abstracts and when available publisher article content. Not a 2101-DOI global reset and not an authoritative new formal review.

rows.primaryContribution: Ru/W0.4ZrOx-catalyzed consecutive decarboxylation converts waste PET to benzene and controls substrate/catalyst selectivity
rows.preparativeTransformation: PET-derived aromatic polycarboxylate C8 framework -> benzene C6 (reported 83.3% benzene yield)
rows.generalityEvidence: Primary abstract confirms treatment of multiple real-world PET waste streams, not necessarily distinct chemical substrates. Publisher's SI listing explicitly says supporting tables S1-S40 include 'substrate extension' as well as product distributions, but table identities, yields and separability were not retrieved.

sourceEvidence.facts: benzene 83.3%, one feedstock class PET and heterogeneous catalyst engineering
SI tables include substrate extension; exact identities unknown

rows.boundaryChallenge: The existing exclusion describes a single PET waste stream, but supplementary materials explicitly mention substrate extension. This cannot be dismissed without the actual substrate table. Product type, catalyst vs chemistry novelty and isolated scope remain the deciding facts.
evidenceNeeded: Obtain actual SI substrate-extension table and product distribution/isolated production data
Determine whether distinct aromatic polycarboxylates beyond PET are converted through a transferable synthesis
rows.nextAction: Reassess against general substrate-to-product scope in dedicated prepublication recheck; do not change formal exclude without evidence.

rows.primaryContribution: Integrated eCO2R with CO-tolerant Pd phosphinosulfonate-borane catalysts for ethylene oligomerization and ethylene–CO copolymerization into hydrocarbons
rows.preparativeTransformation: Ethylene/CO gas -> CO–ethylene solid copolymer and internal olefin oligomers C4-C28; publisher body explicitly states 34 mg isolated alternating copolymer and experiments with several Ar phosphinosulfonate variants
rows.generalityEvidence: Publisher section 2.1 varies aryl-phosphine substituents and olefin distribution/CO tolerance; monomer/organic substrate diversity beyond ethylene/CO not established. These are actual polymer chemistry experiments, not merely an incidental single fuel readout.

sourceEvidence.type: indexed original ACS article body section 2.1, Scheme 1, Figure 2
sourceEvidence.facts: Pd catalyst structures and oligomer distributions; 34 mg isolated copolymer in test; integrated CO2 fuels process
C4-C28 hydrocarbons, CO-tolerant ligand catalyst, fuels target

rows.boundaryChallenge: An integrated energy-process paper can still have a genuine new polymerization catalysis contribution. However, borane-adduct Pd phosphinosulfonates were previously used for oligomerization; need determine whether novelty is merely CO-tolerant reactor integration rather than general new synthesis mode.
evidenceNeeded: Confirm novelty relative to cited Pd phosphinosulfonate/borane oligomerization literature
Determine scope of isolated oligomers/polymers and whether catalytic mode is general beyond impure single monomer feed
rows.nextAction: Perform scope-specific secondary reading of catalyst comparison and SI; no offslot promotion.

rows.primaryContribution: Electrochemically switch Scholl aromatic C–C cyclodehydrogenation between arenium and radical-cation paths
rows.preparativeTransformation: 3,3'-diphenyl-2,2'-binaphthalene electrocatalytic regimes can give different products; tetracene-derived substrate undergoes arenium-path cyclodehydrogenation
rows.generalityEvidence: Abstract explicitly states 'most substrates can react via both pathways', but only concrete representative product examples are reported in the abstract. Distinguish multiscaffold controlled synthesis versus experiments mainly proving intermediates.

sourceEvidence.facts: LPA vs HPN pathway switching, two described substrates, corrected computational assignment

rows.boundaryChallenge: Pathway-switchable products may be synthetically valuable, but the primary thesis is mechanistic re-assignment. Substrate scope and isolated product generality from SI are necessary to classify as new organic synthesis rather than pure mechanistic study.
evidenceNeeded: Original SI examples, isolated yields and structural products for LPA vs HPN across substrate classes
rows.nextAction: Read SI tables before changing exclusion; respect original publication date.

rows.primaryContribution: Support-crystal-phase engineering in Ir/Nb2O5 determines carbonyl-selective hydrogenation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes
rows.preparativeTransformation: α,β-unsaturated aldehydes -> unsaturated allylic alcohols by selective C=O hydrogenation
rows.generalityEvidence: Publisher/metadata abstract describes aldehydes in plural and selective product class, but no article-specific substrate table, isolated yields or structural diversity was retrieved.

sourceEvidence.facts: Ir supported on Nb2O5 crystal phase, EMSI, H2 spillover, carbonyl over alkene hydrogenation

rows.boundaryChallenge: Main contribution is catalyst interface design, but published text does not rule out real preparative series; avoid asserting 'no extra substrate examples' until SI checked.
evidenceNeeded: Publisher/SI organic substrate-scope and isolation table
rows.nextAction: Resolve existence and breadth of separate aldehyde products before confirm/overturn exclude.

rows.primaryContribution: ZnOx/black silicon photocathode interface charge buffering to improve photoelectrochemical oxime selectivity
rows.preparativeTransformation: Cyclohexanone plus electrogenerated nitrogen-centered intermediates -> cyclohexanone oxime
rows.generalityEvidence: Actual abstract provides 94.6% Faradaic efficiency and 99.9% cyclohexanone-to-oxime selectivity, which are not separable products or substrate generality; no distinct oxime scope established.

sourceEvidence.facts: single cyclohexanone oxime benchmark, photoelectrode engineering and kinetic design

rows.boundaryChallenge: A real C–N product exists; main advance is electrode interfacial electron kinetics and single target production rather than general organic preparation.
rows.nextAction: Reopen only if new SI substrate/product series is verified.

rows.primaryContribution: MOF interpenetration transformations align diacetylene units for solid-state topochemical polymerization with nonlinear optical performance
rows.preparativeTransformation: Diacetylene units in CAS-22 MOF undergo thermally induced solid-state 1,4-addition polymerization
rows.generalityEvidence: True polymerization is explicitly present, but evidence describes one family of interpenetrated MOFs and links polymerization to optical coefficient (~69x versus CAS-20), not transferable monomer/chain sequence synthetic utility.
rows.boundaryChallenge: The occurrence of a covalent polymerization is acknowledged; the article primarily solves MOF alignment and device property, and broad preparative range remains unsupported.
rows.nextAction: Keep prior scope decision unless distinct transferable polymerization series is evidenced.

rows.primaryContribution: Electron/proton dual modulation of M–N–C single-atom catalysts for O2 activation and lignin breakdown
rows.preparativeTransformation: Native birch lignin oxidative bond cleavage reduces molecular weight and breaks β-O-4, β-β, β-5 linkages
rows.generalityEvidence: Reported generality is metal active site Mn,Co,Ni,Cu,Sn,Ir,Pt, not a broad class of isolated aromatic synthesis products. The abstract identifies reduced molecular weight rather than separable product panel.

sourceEvidence.facts: O2 activation 2.8-fold Vmax, 7 alternative metal active sites, birch lignin cleavage

rows.boundaryChallenge: Lignin chemical cleavage is real, and metal variation is real; however general catalyst performance is not equivalent to general small-molecule preparation.
rows.nextAction: Only revise if downstream product isolation and diverse substrate-to-product preparation are demonstrated.

rows.primaryContribution: Bench-stable Rh/Chiraphos complex advances recyclability and mechanism of citral asymmetric hydrogenation in l-menthol industrial route
rows.generalityEvidence: Existing abstract gives over 10 recycles and TON up to 10,000 for citral; those are catalyst performance, not distinct organic substrates or general scope.

sourceEvidence.facts: citral, air-stable Rh catalyst, 10 recycles and mechanistic head-group recognition

rows.boundaryChallenge: Meaningful industrial stereoselective organic reaction exists, but article-specific generality remains one citral transformation, with catalyst stability central.
rows.nextAction: Retain exclusion absent actual broad synthetic route or substrate range.

rows.preparativeTransformation: Syn triethyltruxene on Cu(111) -> surface-adsorbed iso[4]triangulene; anti form yields a defective structure
rows.generalityEvidence: Surface STM/AFM characterization and single-member iso[n]triangulene family; no isolated broadly usable building blocks or preparative scale.

sourceEvidence.facts: Cu(111) cycloaromatization and planar chirality from one tailored precursor

rows.boundaryChallenge: Novel chemical C–C transformations genuinely occur; their context is single surface-adsorbed nanographene and fundamental electronic structure.

rows.primaryContribution: Protein residue position and electric-field mechanism govern polyurethane-hydrolyzing urethanase
rows.preparativeTransformation: PU chain hydrolysis and low molecular weight dicarbamate hydrolysis by enzyme mutants
rows.generalityEvidence: Actually contains two substrate contexts and substrate-dependent mutagenesis, so do not assert absence of any distinct substrates; however primary output is protein mechanistic design, not preparative isolated organic products.

sourceEvidence.facts: UMG-SP2 loop mutations, QM/MM/MD, low-MW dicarbamate and PU depolymerization

rows.boundaryChallenge: Enzyme catalytic transformations are real and eligible as a category, but variant optimization and degradation assays here do not establish synthetic scope.
rows.nextAction: No change absent actual preparative product scope.
